name: Penken-Joch
kurzbeschreibung: Penkenjoch at 2,095 metres above Mayrhofen blends outdoor adventure, the iconic rhomboid Garnet Chapel, and sweeping views of glaciated Zillertal summits.
preis: Free access to trails (Mayrhofner Bergbahnen cable cars charge fares)
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round; summer lift operations from late May to mid-October
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Penkenjoch, towering at an elevation of 2,095 metres above Mayrhofen in the upper Zillertal, stands as an extraordinarily versatile mountain plateau combining alpine tranquility and modern outdoor recreation. Positioned seamlessly between the Tux and Zillertal valleys, the expansive summit ridge commands peerless panoramas across the icefields of the High Alps Nature Park Zillertal Alps. A crowning architectural marvel is the futuristic Garnet Chapel (Granatkapelle), masterminded by celebrated Swiss architect Mario Botta in the crystalline shape of a faceted garnet stone above an idyllic mountain reservoir. Renowned in winter for the 'Harakiri'—Austria's steepest groomed ski slope—summer transforms the Penkenjoch into a bustling paradise for hikers, paragliders, via ferrata enthusiasts, and families.

Route & Anforderungen

Penkenjoch is made universally accessible by cutting-edge alpine transport. In Mayrhofen, the advanced 3S Penkenbahn funitel whisks visitors upward, linking with chairlifts to the summit ridge; alternatively, the Finkenberger Almbahn ascends from the Tux Valley. At the summit, well-surfaced stroller-friendly pathways loop around the emerald reservoir to the chapel. For adventurous climbers, the limestone towers of the Knorren feature diverse via ferrata routes (grades B to E) equipped with safety cables and footholds. Scenic high-altitude traverses lead towards the Wanglalm or onwards to the Rastkogel Hut. Sturdy hiking shoes with dependable grip and windproof jackets are recommended for all ridge treks.

Besuch & Anreise

Road travel proceeds from motorway A12 via the Wiesing exit along the Zillertal highway (B169) directly into Mayrhofen. Arriving by public transit is effortless via the scenic Zillertalbahn railway from Jenbach straight to Mayrhofen terminal, followed by a short pleasant stroll through town to the Penkenbahn base. Parking garages and lots are provided at the valley lift stations in Mayrhofen and Finkenberg. Summer cable cars operate daily between approximately 8:30 and 17:00.

Tipps

Step inside the Garnet Chapel to experience the intimate, contemplative atmosphere created by filtered skylight illuminating warm geometric larch timber surfaces. Paragliders frequently launch from the ridge, providing colorful spectacles against the glistening backdrop of the Hintertux Glacier.
